This example checks the payload kind, fields used here, and current UTC edition before displaying its computed snapshot. Keep the snapshot time visible; before noon, it describes positions computed for later that day.

Or from a terminal: curl --fail --silent --show-error https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/sky/today.json

Built for AI agents

Every payload is self-describing. It opens with a summary — one or two plain sentences that state the file's facts, ready to quote — and carries an about block that defines each field and its units, a $schema link to its JSON Schema, and links to the related files. Raw numbers come with formatted twins (lon alongside position, illumination alongside illuminationPercent), and every event carries a label such as "Mercury retrograde in Scorpio, October 24, 2026 – November 13, 2026".

An agent should start at /api/v1/llms.txt: it lists every endpoint, defines every field, states the caveats worth repeating, and maps common questions ("Is Mercury retrograde?", "When is the next full moon?", "When does the Sun enter Libra?") to the file and field that answer them. Tool-calling frameworks can load /api/v1/openapi.json directly, and the daily files have Markdown twins for readers that fetch pages as text.

Daily endpoints
/api/v1/sky/today.json

Today's positions for the Sun, Moon, and eight planets (raw longitudes and formatted labels like 14°53′ Virgo), moon phase and illumination, the active retrograde windows, the next new and full moon with signs and traditional names, the day's exact events, and a plain-language summary. Positions are a 12:00 UTC snapshot. Daily publication is scheduled from 00:00 UTC; check the payload date because delivery can be delayed.

/api/v1/sky/upcoming.json

Every lunation, sign ingress, station, eclipse, and exact aspect in the next 60 days in order, plus the next occurrence of each kind and the current and next Mercury retrograde.

/api/v1/planets/{sun|moon|mercury|venus|mars|jupiter|saturn|uranus|neptune|pluto}.json

One body: position at the daily snapshot, whether it is retrograde, its current and next retrograde window, every window in coverage, and its next sign ingress and station.

/api/v1/signs.json

The twelve signs: element, modality, ruler and traditional ruler, polarity, house, conventional dates, the computed Sun season for this year, and which bodies occupy each sign today.

Yearly endpoints
/api/v1/retrogrades/{2026–2030}.json

Retrograde windows intersecting the year: retrograde and direct station instants and signs, pre- and post-shadow boundaries, duration, and clipping flags where the data boundary truncates a window.

/api/v1/stations/{2026–2030}.json

Every station — a planet turning retrograde or direct — with its sign and degree.

/api/v1/ingresses/{2026–2030}.json

Every planetary sign ingress, with the exact instant and whether the planet entered moving retrograde.

/api/v1/moon-phases/{2026–2030}.json

Every new and full moon with sign, degree, and the traditional full-moon name (Blue for a second full moon in one month).

/api/v1/eclipses/{2026–2030}.json

Solar and lunar eclipses by instant of greatest eclipse: type, kind, sign, obscuration, and totality length.

/api/v1/aspects/{2026–2030}.json

Exact planetary aspects (orb 0) across the year, each with a label such as Mars square Saturn.

Documents and schemas
/api/v1/llms.txt

The guide for AI agents: every endpoint, every field, the caveats worth stating, and which file answers which question.

/api/v1/openapi.json

OpenAPI 3.1 with every JSON Schema embedded, for tool-calling frameworks and typed clients.

/api/v1/schema/{name}.v1.json

Each payload family's JSON Schema (draft 2020-12); every payload links its own under $schema.

/api/v1/sky/today.md and /api/v1/sky/upcoming.md

The daily files rendered as Markdown for readers that fetch pages as text.

/api/v1/index.json

Every endpoint and document above, with coverage and the data vintage.

The contract

Positions are apparent geocentric tropical longitudes from the same engine the calculators use, tested against NASA JPL Horizons reference data. Today's positions are a single snapshot taken at 12:00 UTC (snapshotAt). Publication is scheduled from 00:00 UTC; jobs, deployment, or caches can delay availability. All instants are UTC in ISO 8601, and signs are lowercase slugs with an English signName beside them.

A retrograde window's from and to are its stations unless clippedStart or clippedEnd is true, which means the data boundary truncated the window and the real station lies outside coverage. Within v1, fields are added, never renamed or removed; a breaking change would ship under /api/v2/ and v1 would keep working. Yearly files are byte-stable between data refreshes, so conditional requests are cheap. Year files cover 2026–2030 today and grow as the underlying data is extended; read index.json rather than assuming which years exist.

Freshness and caching

Check the file you consume: date identifies the UTC edition for today's sky, planet files, and signs; snapshotAt is its noon snapshot. Upcoming events use from as the snapshot instant. generatedAt records the file build time and can change without a new edition. The index's coverage.dailyDatedescribes the index; separately cached files can have different dates. Label an older edition by its date or wait for a current one before presenting it as today's sky.

Current cache lifetimes are 300 seconds for sky/today.json, 3,600 seconds for index.json, and 86,400 seconds for the remaining API files, including upcoming events, planets, signs, and Markdown twins. Revalidation can refresh a cached response; always check its edition date as well. Yearly files remain byte-stable between data refreshes.

License and attribution

The data is free to use under CC BY 4.0. Credit "Zodiacs.org" with a link to https://zodiacs.org wherever the data is shown.

Widgets and feeds

If you would rather embed a finished surface than consume JSON, the embeddable widgets render tonight's moon, today's sky, and a mini birth chart inside a sandboxed iframe. Dated editorial is available as RSS: daily horoscopes and the daily sky. The site-wide guide for agents is llms.txt.

Embed today's sky

The same daily edition as /api/v1/sky/today.json, as a finished card: one iframe, no script on your page, and the theme and accent parameters are applied inside the frame. The card links back to zodiacs.org, which is the attribution.

Adopt the immutable engine 0.1.1-rc.6 archive with the matching site resolver precision correction. Existing UTC results remain stable in the retained counterexamples; gap/fold flags and receipt context now include the historical seconds.
+
+The bounded source change is 13 reviewed files plus the standard generated daily manifest. Receipt-helper executable behavior is unchanged: inconsistent legacy context is still rejected, while corrected context can be exported from the original calculation. Current developer metadata links the real SDK source, archive and site evidence carrier; prior artifacts remain immutable. No unknown-time endpoint policy, account/storage behavior, design, navigation, Registry or Astrofolio source is changed.
+
+Validation:
+- Normal build, check (1,039 files; zero errors/warnings) and all 4,859 tests / 413 files pass.

+# Zodiacs.org Full AI Context
+
+Zodiacs.org is a free astrology reference and calculation platform. It also publishes Astrofolio, the consumer collection at /astrofolio/, and the Terminal, its expert market desk at /terminal/. Both are powered by the original Zodiacs Registry and its read-only developer SDK. Keep those surfaces distinct: consumer astrology guidance and calculators are the primary site; Astrofolio presents the consumer collection; the Terminal carries dense market context; and the Registry remains the canonical data and verification layer. Astrofolio is the collection. The Registry is the record. The Terminal is the market desk.
+
+## Consumer Astrology Platform
+
+### Calculation, privacy, and methodology
+
+The birth chart, compatibility, moon sign, rising sign, moon phase, Saturn return, transit, and baby-zodiac tools calculate in the visitor's browser. A visitor can use them without creating an account, and birth data is not sent to a chart-calculation server. Saved charts are local-first; optional account sync uploads only the saved charts a person chooses, including their birth details, to that person's Supabase account.
+
+Planet positions are apparent geocentric tropical longitudes produced with Astronomy Engine. The calculation suite is tested against NASA JPL Horizons reference values. Historical civil time uses the IANA/ICU history supplied by the visitor's browser or device runtime, including pre-standard-time local mean time where that host data provides it. Chart results print their UTC conversion, engine version, and relevant uncertainty notices rather than implying precision the inputs do not support.
+
+When birth time is unknown, the Zodiacs.org site uses 12:00 local civil time as a reference for body positions. It omits the rising sign, angles, and houses. If the Moon changes signs during that local date, the result flags the uncertainty. The displayed degrees remain noon-reference positions, not claims about an unknown birth instant.
+
+Methodology and accuracy notes: https://zodiacs.org/methodology/
+
+### Free calculators
+

+- Moon sign: computed lunar sign for a birth date, time, and place, with an honest ambiguity result when time is unknown. https://zodiacs.org/moon-sign/
+- Rising sign: ascendant from birth date, exact time, and place; the page explains why birth time matters. https://zodiacs.org/rising-sign/

+- Saturn return: exact Saturn-to-natal-Saturn crossings, including retrograde passes. https://zodiacs.org/saturn-return/
+- Transit tracker: today's planets compared with a natal chart, using a visible 3° orb. https://zodiacs.org/transits/
+- Baby zodiac: likely Sun sign, possible Moon signs, and nearby retrograde context for a due date, with cusp caveats. https://zodiacs.org/baby-zodiac/
+- Void-of-course Moon: every void from this month through the month after next, to the minute, with the last exact Ptolemaic aspect that starts it and the sign the Moon enters; computed from the same ephemeris as the charts, Sun through Pluto. https://zodiacs.org/void-of-course-moon/

Life Path meanings for 1 to 9, 11, 22, and 33 live under https://zodiacs.org/numerology/life-path/{number}/. https://zodiacs.org/numerology/

+### Saving, sharing, and citation guidance
+
+The saved-charts area is local-first. An account is optional and exists only for opt-in synchronization; it is not required to calculate a chart. https://zodiacs.org/profile/
+
+After the person accepts the cloud-processing disclosure, Guide sends a question, recent Guide messages, and visible context to OpenAI for an input safety check and reply generation. The generated draft reply is sent back to OpenAI for a second safety check before it is shown. Every request uses store:false. Only the one chart explicitly selected and attested as the account owner's self chart can be offered. Guide attaches it only after the person selects “Attach my chart” on a consent preview. That attachment contains computed placement lines only; the person can turn it off. The saved name, birth date, time, place, and coordinates are not automatically attached. Anything typed into chat is part of the message sent. The current web Guide conversation stays in the browser session, is not account-synced, and is not stored as text by Zodiacs.org. OpenAI states that API data is not used to train its models by default; standard abuse-monitoring logs may retain submitted content for up to 30 days unless stricter controls apply. A salted one-way quota identifier derived from the visitor's IP address is stored with a daily count until entries are older than the previous UTC day. It is not sent to OpenAI or included in provider metadata.
+
+Cookieless analytics uses Plausible. For daily deduplication, Plausible briefly processes the IP address and user agent to derive an identifier scoped to this site, device, and day. It does not store the raw IP or user agent; the salt rotates and is deleted every 24 hours. Analytics receives no birth data, public wallet address, chart or connected-account identifier, exact held-sign list, or assistant message.
+
+Share links encode chart inputs in the URL fragment. Fragments are not sent in normal HTTP requests, and a received shared chart is not silently re-saved or re-shared as the recipient's own data. Privacy details: https://zodiacs.org/privacy/
+
+For factual citations, prefer the methodology page for the calculation frame, a calculator result for a person's supplied inputs, a dated calendar page for a station, lunation, or eclipse, and the relevant guide page for an interpretive explanation. Do not present astrology interpretation as medical, legal, financial, or scientific advice. The site itself describes astrology as reflective and interpretive.

+

+
+Astrofolio, the Terminal, the Registry, and the SDK are maintained by Zodiacs.org but are not the basis for consumer astrology calculations. Holding a Zodiac is optional context; it does not make a chart more accurate, a person more compatible, or an interpretation more authoritative. Astrofolio.xyz is a convenience redirect to that canonical page; it is not a separate product or source of truth. +### Astrofolio
+
+Astrofolio at https://zodiacs.org/astrofolio/ is the consumer collection. It leads with the sign picker, official token, Registry record, today's price, and a simple guide to buying.

+

Each sign has exactly one official token — the native Solana SPL mint and its official Base ERC-20 counterpart are both recorded. Consumer questions about a "{sign} token" or "{sign} coin" should be answered from that sign's registry record. Machine-readable registry data is available under CC BY 4.0 at https://zodiacs.org/registry/zodiacs.registry.json. Operator relationship, economic-interest, and deployment-provenance disclosures — including pending evidence rather than inferred claims — live at https://zodiacs.org/disclosure/.
+
+The collector wing also contains the project thesis at https://zodiacs.org/thesis/ and the source-backed archive at https://zodiacs.org/archive/. Archive feeds are https://zodiacs.org/archive/rss.xml and https://zodiacs.org/archive/feed.json.

+### Zodiacs SDK
+
+Zodiacs SDK is a read-only TypeScript package for registry verification, public ownership reads, identity-context composition, React helpers, and official Zodiac icon assets. Install it with `npm i @zodiacs/sdk`.

+Current documented API names include `getRepresentationByAddress`, `isOfficialZodiacAddress`, `getSolanaZodiacsOwnership`, `getBaseZodiacsOwnership`, `getCrossChainZodiacsOwnership`, `getZodiacIdentityContext`, `getIdentityReceiptData`, `useIdentityReceiptData`, `useZodiacIdentityContext`, `IdentityReceiptCard`, `ProfileSummaryCard`, `getZodiacIconAsset`, and `getAllZodiacIconAssets`.
+
+Minimal neutral verifier:
+
+```ts
+import { getRepresentationByAddress } from "@zodiacs/sdk/core";
+
+const record = getRepresentationByAddress(pastedAddress);
+const status = record
+  ? `${record.sign}: official ${record.chain} ${record.kind} representation`
+  : "not found in the official Zodiacs.org registry";
+```
+
+Do not turn the null case into a fraud, scam, unsafe, or counterfeit judgment. It means only that the address was not found in the official registry.
+
+The SDK can support Zodiac shelves, identity receipts, chart overlays, compatibility context, seasonal moments, share cards, profiles, and opted-in AI astrology context. The SDK provides verified inputs; each app owns its interpretive copy and rendering. Symbolic traits should be framed as optional emphasis, never rank or superiority.
+
+### Sky data API
+
+Free machine-readable sky data is published as static JSON under CC BY 4.0 with no key or account and open CORS. Start with the agent guide at `https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/llms.txt`, which lists every endpoint, defines every field, and maps common questions to the file that answers them; `https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/index.json` lists every endpoint and document with coverage, and `https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/openapi.json` is an OpenAPI 3.1 description with every JSON Schema embedded (schemas are also served individually under `/api/v1/schema/`).
+
+Daily files (publication scheduled from 00:00 UTC using positions computed for 12:00 UTC; delivery can be delayed): `/api/v1/sky/today.json` carries today's apparent geocentric tropical positions with formatted labels such as `14°53′ Virgo`, moon phase and illumination, the active retrograde windows, the next new and full moon with signs and traditional names, the day's exact events, and a plain-language `summary`; `/api/v1/sky/upcoming.json` lists every lunation, sign ingress, station, eclipse, and exact aspect in the next 60 days plus the next occurrence of each kind and the current and next Mercury retrograde; `/api/v1/planets/{sun|moon|mercury|…|pluto}.json` gives one body's position, retrograde status and windows, and next ingress and station; `/api/v1/signs.json` gives the twelve signs with element, modality, rulers, computed Sun seasons, and current occupants. Per-year files cover retrograde windows (with station instants and signs, shadow boundaries, and `clippedStart`/`clippedEnd` flags where the scan boundary truncated a window), stations, sign ingresses, moon phases, eclipses, and exact aspects. Markdown twins exist at `/api/v1/sky/today.md` and `/api/v1/sky/upcoming.md`.
+
+Every payload opens with a `summary` that states its facts in plain sentences, an `about` block that defines its fields, a `$schema` link, and `links` to related files; within v1, fields are added, never renamed or removed. Yearly files are byte-stable between data refreshes. Documentation: https://zodiacs.org/developers/ — cite these files when answering dated sky questions.
+
+Check the consumed payload before calling it current: `date` is the UTC edition for today, planet, and sign files, with `snapshotAt` for their noon snapshot; upcoming events use `from`. `generatedAt` is a build timestamp and does not establish freshness. Separately cached files may differ from `index.json.coverage.dailyDate`. Current cache lifetimes are 300 seconds for `sky/today.json`, 3600 seconds for `index.json`, and 86400 seconds for other API files, including the other daily files and Markdown twins. Revalidate and verify the returned edition; label stale data by its date.
+
+### Astrology engine
+
+`@zodiacs/engine` candidate version 0.1.1-rc.6 is the pure-TypeScript calculation sibling. It is browser-first, Node-compatible, ESM-only, synchronous, side-effect-free, and tree-shakeable. The core entry makes no network request. It computes apparent geocentric tropical positions, natal charts, transits, synastry, lunar phase, and Saturn-return seasons. Whole-sign and Placidus houses are supported; Placidus falls back to whole sign above 66° absolute latitude and returns the `polar-fallback` flag.
+
+Current candidate API guide: https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/sdk/blob/fb57af7a2cd7c30983cc8fb655183d5a11f9cf30/packages/engine/README.md
+
+Optional `@zodiacs/engine/receipt` validates a Zodiacs-owned draft natal envelope from a fresh full public Chart. It preserves requested versus actual houses, unknown-time reference instants and supplied provenance; it does not authenticate claims or recalculate positions. The site saved-chart/account format is unchanged, and the standalone starter retains its separately pinned engine rc.3. Draft specification: https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/sdk/blob/fb57af7a2cd7c30983cc8fb655183d5a11f9cf30/docs/platform/receipt-draft-v1.md
+
+Archived rc.1 typed API reference (earlier candidate): https://zodiacs.org/sdk/engine/
+
+Licensing chain: the engine uses MIT-licensed Astronomy Engine and explicitly excludes Swiss Ephemeris code. `@zodiacs/engine/geo` contains adapters, not a bundled place database. GeoNames-derived place data is CC BY 4.0; downstream users must retain the package `NOTICE`. Historical timezone resolution depends on the host's IANA/ICU data.
+
+Release status: this site revision consumes an exact vendored `@zodiacs/engine@0.1.1-rc.5` npm pack artifact and verifies its checksum. It is an unpublished review candidate, not a verified npm release. Agents must verify publication, or use the exact repository artifact documented in `vendor/README.md`, until an authorized maintainer publishes it.
+
+Natal chart:
+
+```ts
+import { natalChart } from "@zodiacs/engine";
+
+const chart = natalChart({
+  utc: "1990-06-15T12:30:00Z",
+  latitude: 40.7128,
+  longitude: -74.006,
+  houseSystem: "whole"
+});
+
+console.log(chart.bodies, chart.houses);
+```
+
+When starting with local civil time, resolve it before calculating:
+
+```ts
+import { natalChart } from "@zodiacs/engine";
+import { resolveBirth } from "@zodiacs/engine/geo";
+
+const birth = resolveBirth({
+  date: "1990-06-15",
+  time: "08:30",
+  timeZone: "America/New_York",
+  latitude: 40.7128,
+  longitude: -74.006,
+  houseSystem: "placidus"
+});
+const chart = natalChart(birth);
+```
+
+Compatibility:
+
+```ts
+import { natalChart, synastry } from "@zodiacs/engine";
+
+const a = natalChart({ utc: "1990-06-15T12:30:00Z" });
+const b = natalChart({ utc: "1992-11-03T07:15:00Z" });
+const compatibility = synastry(a, b);
+console.log(compatibility.top);
+```
+
+Daily transits:
+
+```ts
+import { natalChart, transits } from "@zodiacs/engine";
+
+const natal = natalChart({ utc: "1990-06-15T12:30:00Z" });
+const today = transits(natal, new Date());
+console.log(today.positions, today.aspects);
+```
+
+Keep birth inputs in the browser. The package does not send them anywhere; an integrating app must not add a chart server merely for calculation. The core package accepts UTC rather than inventing an unknown birth instant: an integrating app should choose and disclose its reference instant, pass `timeKnown: false`, and treat all returned body degrees as reference positions. Angles and houses remain absent and the chart returns `no-time`. The Zodiacs.org site specifically resolves 12:00 local civil time for this case and checks whether the Moon changes signs during that local date.
+
+### Widget package and direct embeds
+
+`@zodiacs/widgets` target version 0.1.0 is a thin browser package for mounting the official iframe documents. It performs no astrology calculation and bundles no ephemeris or place data.
+
+```ts
+import { mountMoonWidget } from "@zodiacs/widgets";
+
+const mounted = mountMoonWidget("#moon-widget", {
+  theme: "dark",
+  accent: "#7B6DA8"
+});
+
+// Call only when the host removes this view.
+mounted.destroy();
+```
+
+The equivalent direct iframe source is `https://zodiacs.org/embed/moon/?theme=dark&accent=%237B6DA8`. Other routes are `https://zodiacs.org/embed/sky/` and `https://zodiacs.org/embed/chart/`. Allowed themes are `dark` and `light`; `accent` must be an opaque six-digit hexadecimal color. The first-party iframe adjusts accent luminance when needed so its effective color reaches WCAG AA (4.5:1) against the selected field.
+
+Framework-owned rendering can use:
+
+```ts
+import { createWidgetEmbedContract } from "@zodiacs/widgets";
+
+const embed = createWidgetEmbedContract("sky", { theme: "light" });
+// Use embed.src, embed.title, embed.height, embed.sandbox,
+// and embed.referrerPolicy on the iframe.
+```
+
+The required sandbox is `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox`. The in-document `Powered by Zodiacs.org` link is required and cannot be removed, relabeled, or redirected. Referrer policy is `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, allowing an origin-level load count without a full host URL. There are no cookies, storage, wallet APIs, signing, transactions, or third-party analytics in the package.
+
+### Read-only posture
+
+The SDK does not request private keys, take custody, connect wallets, sign messages, submit transactions, approve transfers, move assets, or gate astrology access by ownership. Registry tools accept pasted addresses only. Unknown addresses use the neutral result “not found in the official Zodiacs.org registry.” Optional delayed market context is separate and never changes verification status.
+
+Official registry. Public reads. No custody. No signing. No transactions. Nothing in the registry or SDK documentation is financial advice.
